posts.title: Charter Demand Is Up 27%. Flying Isn’t
posts.excerpt: Avinode reports U.S. charter demand up 27%. Departures are flat. Both numbers are accurate, and the gap between them matters if you are projecting charter revenue.

posts.title: 617 Aircraft, 21 for Sale: Inside the G550 Market
posts.excerpt: Per JETNET, 617 G550s are in operation and 21 are for sale. Narrow to 2015 and newer and it drops to two. What scarcity looks like when production has ended.

posts.title: Jet A at a Six-Month High: What It Actually Costs
posts.excerpt: Jet A reached $8.36 a gallon in September, up 4.9% in a month and 32.7% since January. The Eastern region saw the steepest rise in the Lower 48.

posts.title: How Exposed Is Business Aviation to the Next Downturn?
posts.excerpt: Flying is up, inventory is tight, and nothing in the data says a downturn has started. But the growth is concentrated in the segment that fell hardest last time, and the wealth behind it tracks equity markets more closely than ever.

posts.title: The Largest Managed Fleet in the World Just Closed. What It Means for Owners.
posts.excerpt: Solairus closed its acquisition of Clay Lacy's management and charter divisions on October 1, creating a 500-aircraft managed fleet. What consolidation at this scale means for the owners involved, and for everyone else.

posts.title: Q3 2026: The Quarter Where the Paperwork Started to Matter
posts.excerpt: Flight activity rose through the third quarter while transactions lagged. A pending tariff decision, a threatened sales ban and a Canadian tax incentive explain most of the gap.

posts.title: Canada’s Proposed 100% Aircraft Expensing: Could It Accelerate the Aircraft Replacement Cycle?
posts.excerpt: Canada’s proposed expansion of 100% immediate expensing to qualifying business aircraft could change the economics of aircraft replacement for Canadian owners. With new and potentially pre-owned aircraft included, the proposal could also create new cross-border demand for U.S. business jet inventory.

posts.title: Why We Publish Market Notes
posts.excerpt: Private aviation runs on incomplete information. These notes come out of transactions we have actually worked on.

posts.title: The Light Jet Market in 2026: Why Smaller Business Jets Could Lead the Next Decade
posts.excerpt: The private jet market remains active in 2026, but some of its most interesting opportunities are emerging in the light-jet segment. With tight late-model inventory, strong utilization, practical operating economics, and forecasts calling for significant long-term growth, smaller business jets are becoming an increasingly important part of private aviation.

posts.title: Pilatus PC-12 NGX: A Modern Look at the Most Capable Turboprop in the Sky
posts.excerpt: The Pilatus PC-12 NGX represents the latest evolution of the world’s most successful single-engine turboprop — a versatile aircraft known for reliability, efficiency, and astonishing runway performance. With a redesigned avionics suite, smarter engine management, and a refined cabin experience, the NGX pushes the productivity of turboprop ownership to a new level. This up-close look explores why the aircraft continues to dominate its category in 2025.

posts.title: September 11 and the Evolution of Private Aviation
posts.excerpt: Twenty-five years after September 11, its effects remain deeply woven into American aviation. From changing security expectations to increased interest in charter and fractional aviation, September 11 reshaped how people think about flying—and reinforced the importance of trust, continuity, and relationships throughout private aviation.

posts.title: Bombardier, U.S. Market Access and What Trump’s Latest Restrictions Could Mean for Private Aviation
posts.excerpt: President Trump’s latest threat to restrict Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States introduces a new variable into the private jet market. Penn Jets examines what the developing dispute could mean for Challenger and Global buyers, existing owners, pre-owned values, and competing manufacturers.

posts.title: How to Buy Your First Private Jet: 2025 Step-by-Step Buyer’s Guide
posts.excerpt: Buying your first private jet is one of the most rewarding—and complex—investments you’ll ever make. This guide walks you through every step of the process, from defining your mission and building the right team to financing, inspections, and operational setup. Whether you’re purchasing solo or exploring fractional ownership, Penn Jets’ 10-step roadmap helps you avoid common pitfalls and launch your ownership journey with confidence.

posts.title: Sustainable Aviation: The Future of Private Flying
posts.excerpt: Private aviation is entering a new era — one defined by innovation, efficiency, and environmental responsibility. Once criticized for its carbon footprint, the industry is now leading the charge toward cleaner skies through Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), hybrid-electric propulsion, and hydrogen-powered aircraft. Major players like NetJets and Otto Aviation are proving that luxury flight and sustainability can coexist, ushering in a future where private jets symbolize not just status, but stewardship.

posts.title: The State of the Private Jet Market In Q3 2025
posts.excerpt: The private jet market closed Q3 2025 on a strong note, with flight activity rebounding, OEM deliveries climbing, and pre-owned inventory tightening for newer models. Gulfstream, Textron, and Embraer all reported solid delivery gains, while dealer confidence and transaction volume rose across the board. Prices have stabilized—firm for late-model jets, more negotiable for older aircraft—creating a balanced environment for both buyers and sellers. With fractional programs booming and charter rates holding steady, private aviation is entering Q4 with renewed momentum and long-term confidence.

posts.title: Jet Charter vs. Ownership: Making the Right Choice
posts.excerpt:
A personal look inside private aviation from someone who’s lived it. Learn the real costs, control, and lifestyle differences between owning and chartering a jet — and how the right structure can turn an aircraft from an expense into a strategic investment.
